speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance and distribution of the rash, and for how long have these symptoms persisted? Have you noticed any changes in the skin texture or color, such as thickening or hyperpigmentation?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of contact with cattle or other livestock, and have you noticed any skin changes on your hands or feet, such as hyperkeratosis or fissures? I need to determine if this exposure is linked to a potential zoonotic infection like Erysipelothrix rhusiopathides.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a pruritic rash, neuropathy, and specifically the loss of eyebrows and eyelashes (madarosis) strongly suggests Hansen's disease. REQUEST TEST: Acid-Fast Bacilli Smear and Skin Biopsy for Mycobacterium leprae.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy: Chronic inflammatory cells with features suggestive of leprosy. Nerve Conduction Studies: Reduced sensory nerve action potentials in the ulnar nerves. Serology: Anti-PGL-1 antibodies Positive.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as a farmer, no history of travel outside the local area.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in vision, or any respiratory symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of hypopigmented macules, madarosis, and bilateral palmar neuropathy is classic for leprosy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hansen's disease
